title: Analytics observability: SLI decomposition, trace propagation, and cost-aware alerting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create a pragmatic, low-friction observability foundation for the analytics ingestion and processing pipeline that enables reliable SLI/SLO measurement, end-to-end traceability across streaming and batch components, and cost-aware alerting for high-cardinality metrics. This ticket scopes SLI decomposition, trace context propagation strategy, sampling policy, logging hygiene, dashboard requirements, and a staged rollout plan for migrating existing ad-hoc metrics to the unified SLI catalog.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Define a canonical SLI catalog for analytics services with at least: ingest_p95_latency, processing_success_rate (5m), event_completeness_ratio (per-source), downstream_freshness_seconds (p99)
A2: Instrument OpenTelemetry trace propagation through Kafka consumer -> Beam pipeline -> enrichment services -> storage, with trace_id present in logs and dashboard links
A3: Implement a sampling strategy (default head-based 100% sampling on errors, 5% for success traces, tail-sampling flag for latency spikes) and document CPU/memory impact in benchmark notes
A4: Provide Grafana dashboards for SLI heatmaps, per-tenant top-N error sources, and a combined SLO error budget panel with burn-rate alerts
A5: Migration plan and data backfill strategy documented; rollback plan validated in staging and smoke-tested with synthetic traffic
technical_notes: We will use OpenTelemetry SDKs already in service runtime; add instrumentations for Kafka consumers and Beam DoFns where missing.
Trace context must be propagated using W3C Traceparent and b3 as fallback for legacy connectors.
Logging format: structured JSON with fields: trace_id, span_id, tenant_id, event_type, pipeline_stage, latency_ms. Redact PII at ingestion boundary.
Metrics ingestion: route SLI metrics to prometheus-compatible pushgateway for short-lived batch jobs; use long-lived collectors for streaming services.
Sampling: implement adaptive tail-sampling controller in ingestion plane to increase sampling during p95/p99 latency anomalies.
We need to add cost tags to each metric emission (e.g., model_variant, quantization_level) so dashboards can surface cost per SLI unit later.
decisions: D1: Adopt W3C traceparent as primary trace context format to align with external integrations.
D2: Default success-trace sampling at 5% to limit storage cost; errors and traces with latency > p95 sampled at 100%.
D3: Use a central SLI registry (YAML catalog in repo) instead of ad-hoc metric names to allow automated dashboard generation.
D4: Do not attempt full per-tenant raw-event retention for observability; rely on sampled traces + aggregated metrics for high-cardinality tenants to control costs.
tradeoffs: T1: Lower sampling reduces storage and cost but reduces ability to debug intermittent skews for small tenants.
T2: Adding tracing to Beam transforms increases CPU overhead; we mitigate by selective instrumentation and sampling thresholds.
T3: Pushing batch job metrics via pushgateway is less real-time than streaming metrics but avoids heavyweight per-job collectors.
rollout_plan: R1: Spike in staging: enable full tracing + 100% sampling for synthetic traffic, validate context propagation and dashboard panels (2 days)
R2: Canary in prod: enable tracing for 10% of traffic for a non-critical tenant slice, monitor throughput and storage impact (3 days)
R3: Gradual increase: expand to 25% then to default 5% sampling for successes, 100% for errors; enable adaptive tail-sampling after stability check (1 week)
R4: Migrate existing ad-hoc SLIs to catalog and replace dashboard panels using generated queries; keep legacy panels as read-only for 2 weeks then retire.

Benchmarks collected (summary):
- Staging full-trace CPU delta: +8% on ingest nodes
- Storage projection: 1TB/day @100% success sampling; 0.28TB/day @5% + adaptive tail-sampling
- Query latency impact on metrics store negligible for aggregated SLI queries
